affectedSurfaces: agent harness project and workspace identity propagation
browser authenticated context ownership and teardown
hypothesis: Propagating canonical project identity separately from execution cwd, and binding direct workflow tool calls to invocation-scoped session cleanup, lets the browser module isolate authenticated contexts by scope and session without weakening existing tool policy or approval controls.

metricsCompared.name: authenticated browser context ownership
metricsCompared.baseline: One process-global context and current page could be reused across every hosted scope and session.
metricsCompared.candidate: Lifecycle regressions prove separate contexts and pages for each scope/session identity and exact-session teardown.

metricsCompared.name: canonical project identity propagation
metricsCompared.baseline: Tool and harness execution exposed cwd without a distinct canonical project directory, so worktree execution could resolve browser profiles against the wrong tree.
metricsCompared.candidate: Classic loop, workflow, nested-agent, REPL, Telegram, approval, inbound-signal, and browser regressions preserve projectDir separately from workspace cwd.

metricsCompared.name: focused security regressions
metricsCompared.baseline: No regression exercised cross-scope browser state reuse or workflow direct-tool cleanup.
metricsCompared.candidate: The browser suite passes 83 tests and focused core/operator suites cover invocation identity, nested parallel/foreach propagation, symlink-safe profile ownership, and exact teardown.

rationale: The candidate closes the confirmed high-severity cross-scope browser-state leak at both required boundaries: hosted execution now carries canonical scope/project and invocation-session identity, while the browser lifecycle keys live state by scope plus session and resolves profile ownership from canonical filesystem targets. Focused regressions cover scope/session separation, worktree cwd divergence, REPL and Telegram operator paths, external and symlink-escaping profile ownership, direct workflow-tool teardown, and distinct session propagation through parallel children and concurrent foreach items. Authorization, approval, tool-risk, secret handling, and injection-defense behavior are unchanged.
